articles.title: Boeing Receives $2.82 Billion Air Force Modification For 15 KC-46A Tankers
articles.snippet:
Boeing Defense, Space & Security received a $2.82 billion U.S. Air Force contract modification covering 15 KC-46A Pegasus aerial refueling aircraft. The aircraft are part of Lot 13, a production batch under Boeing’s existing KC-46A contract. The modification also covers G081, subscriptions and licenses.
The post Boeing Receives $2.82 Billion Air Force Modification For 15 KC-46A Tankers appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Boeing Receives $2.82 Billion Air Force Modification For 15 KC-46A Tankers
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 2:42 PM
Boeing Receives $2.82 Billion Air Force Modification For 15 KC-46A Tankers
Boeing Defense, Space & Security received a $2.82 billion U.S. Air Force contract modification covering 15 KC-46A Pegasus aerial refueling aircraft. The aircraft are part of Lot 13, a production batch under Boeing’s existing KC-46A contract. The modification also covers G081, subscriptions and licenses.
The Air Force obligated the full $2,819,046,560 at award using fiscal 2027 aircraft procurement funds. That amount covers the entire package, including the items awarded alongside the aircraft. The announcement did not break out the cost of the aircraft or the other items, so it provides no standalone price per tanker.
Boeing will perform the work in Seattle, Washington, with completion expected by June 30, 2030. That date applies to the work covered by the modification. The award announcement did not provide a delivery schedule for individual aircraft or identify the units that will receive them.
The KC-46A Pegasus is an aerial refueling aircraft that allows other aircraft to take on fuel in flight. Lot 13 adds another batch to the Air Force’s acquisition of the tanker. The fiscal 2027 funding identifies the appropriation used for the award, while the June 2030 completion date reflects the work schedule.
The Air Force identified FA8625-11-C-6600 as the existing contract being modified and assigned FA8609-27-C-B002 to the action for administrative purposes. Both numbers refer to the same $2.82 billion action. The original number identifies the underlying KC-46A contract, and the new number identifies the Lot 13 modification in the award notice.
The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity. Boeing Defense, Space & Security, a division of The Boeing Company, is the contractor responsible for the Seattle work. The announced award value applies specifically to the 15-aircraft production lot and its accompanying items, and the notice did not give a new cumulative value for the underlying KC-46A contract.

articles.title: RTX’s Pratt & Whitney Receives $2.53 Billion Navy Action For F-35 Engine Sustainment
articles.snippet:
RTX's Pratt & Whitney received a $2.53 billion U.S. Navy contract action to sustain the F135 engines that power F-35 Lightning II aircraft. The award covers maintenance and repair at operating units and depots, as well as services and spare parts for U.S. military branches, international program partners and Foreign Military Sales customers.
The post RTX’s Pratt & Whitney Receives $2.53 Billion Navy Action For F-35 Engine Sustainment appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
RTX’s Pratt & Whitney Receives $2.53 Billion Navy Action For F-35 Engine Sustainment
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 2:40 PM
RTX’s Pratt & Whitney Receives $2.53 Billion Navy Action For F-35 Engine Sustainment
RTX’s Pratt & Whitney received a $2.53 billion U.S. Navy contract action to sustain the F135 engines that power F-35 Lightning II aircraft. The award covers maintenance and repair at operating units and depots, as well as services and spare parts for U.S. military branches, international program partners and Foreign Military Sales customers.
The work includes engineering, logistics, software sustainment and technical data updates. Pratt & Whitney will also provide training, manage support equipment and supply replenishment spare parts. The Navy expects the work to conclude in November 2027.
The Navy identified $436.67 million in funding to be obligated at award, about 17% of the announced contract action value. Fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance accounts will provide $147.49 million from the Air Force, $33.91 million from the Navy and $80.46 million from the Marine Corps. F-35 cooperative program partners will provide $99.43 million, and Foreign Military Sales funds will account for another $75.38 million.
East Hartford, Connecticut, accounts for the largest share of the work at 40%, followed by Oklahoma City at 21% and Indianapolis at 12%. Together, the three sites account for 73% of the effort. Additional U.S. work will take place in West Palm Beach, Florida, Windsor Locks, Connecticut, and Fort Worth, Texas. Overseas work will take place in Norway, the Netherlands, Japan, Australia, Italy and the United Kingdom.
The Navy issued the award as an undefinitized contract action, which allows work to begin while the parties finalize contract terms. The contract contains cost-plus-fixed-fee, cost-plus-incentive-fee, cost and fixed-price-incentive-fee line items. Those arrangements allow the Navy to apply different payment and incentive terms to different portions of the sustainment work.
The Navy issued the action without competition. Naval Air Systems Command at Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity. The contract number is N0001926C0112.

articles.title: VINCI Takes Majority Stake In LISEA At €2.1 Billion Valuation
articles.snippet:
VINCI Concessions has acquired an additional 8% stake in LISEA, raising its ownership to 50.04% and making it the majority shareholder in the company that holds the concession for France’s South Europe Atlantic high-speed rail line. The acquisition follows Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations’ decision to sell its stake.
The post VINCI Takes Majority Stake In LISEA At €2.1 Billion Valuation appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
VINCI Takes Majority Stake In LISEA At €2.1 Billion Valuation
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 2:38 PM
VINCI Takes Majority Stake In LISEA At €2.1 Billion Valuation
VINCI Concessions has acquired an additional 8% stake in LISEA, raising its ownership to 50.04% and making it the majority shareholder in the company that holds the concession for France’s South Europe Atlantic high-speed rail line. The acquisition follows Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations’ decision to sell its stake.
The transaction values all of LISEA’s equity at €2.1 billion. VINCI said it will continue to account for its stake under the equity method, which records its share of LISEA’s earnings without consolidating the concessionaire’s results line by line.
LISEA Builds Maintenance Capacity For New Rail Operators
More than 175 million passenger journeys have been made on the line since it opened in July 2017. VINCI sees room for growth as France opens its rail services market to greater competition. For LISEA, that means preparing to serve new train operators, including providing a place to maintain and store their fleets.
LISEA has begun construction on what VINCI describes as France’s first independent train maintenance and stabling facility. The site is in Marcheprime, near Bordeaux, and is scheduled for completion at the end of 2027. It will service and store rail operator Velvet’s new trainsets starting in 2028. The facility will give new operators access to a depot for work and storage between passenger services.
VINCI Expects Limited Impact From Potential Tax Increase
VINCI said a potential increase in France’s tax on the operation of long-distance transport infrastructure would have a limited impact on the concession. The increase is under consideration as part of France’s 2027 finance bill.
The additional stake gives VINCI Concessions a narrow majority in an operating rail asset as LISEA builds the depot for new operators. The ownership change and the depot project are separate developments, with the new facility expected to begin supporting Velvet the year after construction is scheduled to finish.

articles.title: Northrop Grumman Receives $1.147 Billion Across Two Navy Aircraft Awards
articles.snippet:
Northrop Grumman Systems received two U.S. Navy contract actions with a combined announced value of $1.147 billion. The larger award funds development work for the E-130J strategic communications aircraft, while a separate order provides technical support for E-2C and E-2D aircraft operated by international customers.
The post Northrop Grumman Receives $1.147 Billion Across Two Navy Aircraft Awards appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Northrop Grumman Receives $1.147 Billion Across Two Navy Aircraft Awards
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 2:33 PM
Northrop Grumman Receives $1.147 Billion Across Two Navy Aircraft Awards
Northrop Grumman Systems received two U.S. Navy contract actions with a combined announced value of $1.147 billion. The larger award funds development work for the E-130J strategic communications aircraft, while a separate order provides technical support for E-2C and E-2D aircraft operated by international customers.
The $1.130 billion cost-plus-incentive-fee modification exercises options for Northrop Grumman to design, develop and deliver three E-130J system demonstration test articles and initial spare parts. The work supports the program’s engineering and manufacturing development phase. The E-130J will use government-furnished C-130J-30 aircraft to modernize the Navy’s Take Charge and Move Out strategic communications mission.
The Navy will initially obligate $4.18 million for the E-130J work from fiscal 2027 research, development, test and evaluation funds. Melbourne, Florida, accounts for 35% of the work, followed by Marietta, Georgia, at 23% and Richardson, Texas, at 15%. Those three locations account for 73% of the effort. The Navy expects work under the modification to conclude in January 2030 and issued it as P00018 under contract N0001925C0130.
The separate $16.41 million cost-plus-fixed-fee order covers in-service and technical support for E-2C and E-2D aircraft for Foreign Military Sales customers in France, Japan, Taiwan and Egypt. Its scope covers requirements shared across the aircraft as well as those specific to individual customers. The Navy will obligate approximately $6.65 million in Foreign Military Sales funds at award.
Northrop Grumman will perform about 64% of the E-2 work in Melbourne. The remaining work will take place in Lorient and Cuers, France, Misawa and Tokyo, Japan, Pingtung, Taiwan, and Cairo, Egypt. The Navy expects the support work to continue through October 2033.
Naval Air Systems Command at Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity for both actions. Initial funding across the two awards totals approximately $10.83 million. The E-2 support order, N0001927F1065, was issued under basic ordering agreement N0001925G0003.

articles.title: EBRD announces up to $520m for Jordan’s desalination and water carrier project
articles.snippet: EBRD announces up to $520m for Jordan’s desalination and water carrier project London Daily News
articles.text:
Listen to this article
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has announced financing of up to $520 million for a desalination and water transport project intended to strengthen Jordan’s drinking water supply.
The package, announced on 26 November, combines a senior loan of up to $475 million from the bank with a loan of up to $45 million from ILX Fund. It will support the Aqaba-Amman Water Desalination and Conveyance project, also known as the National Water Carrier.
The EBRD values the overall scheme at $6.7 billion. Its lending package forms part of a wider $4.5 billion debt financing arrangement involving international financial institutions and local banks, rather than covering the full cost of the project.
Once operational, the infrastructure is expected to meet about 40% of Jordan’s municipal water needs and directly benefit approximately 4.3 million people, according to the EBRD. Those figures describe the bank’s expected impact, not water already being delivered.
Desalination plant and a route to Amman
The financing will contribute to a seawater desalination plant in Aqaba with planned annual capacity of 300 million cubic metres. A 438km conveyance system will carry drinking water from the coastal city to Amman.
The project also includes a dedicated solar photovoltaic plant with peak generating capacity of 281 megawatts. The EBRD said this would meet about 30% of the scheme’s electricity requirements, integrating renewable energy into the operation without providing all of its power needs.
The borrower is the National Carrier Project Company, owned by infrastructure investor Meridiam, Suez International and Jordan’s Social Security Investment Fund. The company signed a 30-year project agreement with the Ministry of Water and Irrigation in January 2025.
The EBRD described the scheme as its first water-desalination public-private partnership. The International Finance Corporation, which is also involved in financing the project, said the company would construct, operate and maintain the infrastructure.
Affordability and pressure on freshwater supplies
Canada is contributing $30 million and Finland €7 million in concessional financing through the EBRD’s High-Impact Partnership on Climate Action. The bank said these contributions were intended to support affordable water charges for end-users.
The announcement does not set out a household tariff or promise a particular reduction in bills. The affordability objective sits alongside the wider aim of creating a more reliable water source and reducing pressure on depleted aquifers.
The International Finance Corporation described Jordan as one of the world’s most water-scarce countries. It put annual available water at 61 cubic metres per person, compared with an absolute water scarcity threshold of 500 cubic metres.
In its separate announcement on 26 November, the corporation said climate pressures and population growth were adding to the strain on existing supplies. The desalination scheme is intended to address that shortage by bringing a new source of drinking water into the system.
Jordan’s water and irrigation minister, Raed Abu Soud, said the government would work with partners to keep implementation on the approved schedule and meet technical and environmental requirements. He placed the project alongside efforts to improve supply efficiency, reduce water losses and diversify sources.

articles.title: Ethiopia Secures $342.4 Million Health Financing as UAE Foundation Expands Africa Investment
articles.snippet: Ethiopia Secures $342.4 Million Health Financing as UAE Foundation Expands Africa Investment Birr Metrics
articles.text:
Ethiopia Secures $342.4 Million Health Financing as UAE Foundation Expands Africa Investment
Yared Seyoum
November 26, 2026
Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation’s 20 million US dollars commitment helped mobilise 322.4 US dollars million in additional government and development partner funding, with 120 health facilities set to receive equipment and essential medicines over three years.
Ethiopia has mobilised 342.4 million US dollars to strengthen maternal, newborn and child healthcare services, following a 20 million US dollars commitment from the Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity that helped unlock additional financing from the government and development partners.
The financing forms part of a broader $135 million investment announced by the UAE-based foundation on November 26, targeting more than 500 health facilities across nine African countries, including Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Ghana, Liberia, Malawi, Sierra Leone and Mozambique.
Announced at the International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA) in Addis Ababa, the continental initiative is expected to attract more than 550 million US dollars in additional funding through matching contributions from participating governments and donors.
Ethiopia accounts for a significant share of the programme's announced commitments. The foundation's 20 million US dollars pledge to the country's Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn and Child Health (RMNCH) Compact helped secure a further 151.2 million US dollars from development partners, which was matched by an equivalent contribution from the Ethiopian government.
The resulting $342.4 million financing package will support around 120 health facilities over three years, providing essential medicines, medical equipment and technologies aimed at improving maternal and newborn care.
Planned investments include artificial intelligence-enabled ultrasound equipment to help healthcare workers identify pregnancy complications, alongside antibiotics to prevent and treat infections, including sepsis.
The financing comes as Ethiopia seeks to strengthen access to essential healthcare services and reduce preventable deaths among mothers, newborns and children. The availability of medical supplies and diagnostic equipment remains a constraint across many African health systems, with only 35 percent of essential medicines available in public health facilities and fewer than one-third of facilities equipped to conduct basic diagnostic tests, according to figures cited by the foundation.
The programme uses a co-financing model that links donor commitments with government spending, requiring participating governments to contribute at least an equivalent amount to the foundation's investment. The approach is intended to align external financing with national health priorities while increasing domestic funding for essential medical supplies.
Ethiopia's Health Minister Mekdes Daba said the compact would strengthen service delivery, improve the availability of essential medicines and reinforce healthcare services for women, newborns and children.
She said the arrangement builds on the government's broader health sector transformation agenda through shared investment and accountability between the government and its development partners.

articles.title: PHINIA Acquires FMP Group’s Asia-Pacific Brake Parts Business In $160 Million Deal Expected To Close In 2027
articles.snippet:
PHINIA has agreed to acquire the core operating assets and brand rights of FMP Group’s automotive aftermarket business in Australia, Thailand and Malaysia for approximately $160 million. The deal would expand PHINIA’s brake components portfolio and give it the right to use the Bendix brand in Australia and certain other Asia-Pacific markets.
The post PHINIA Acquires FMP Group’s Asia-Pacific Brake Parts Business In $160 Million Deal Expected To Close In 2027 appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
PHINIA Acquires FMP Group’s Asia-Pacific Brake Parts Business In $160 Million Deal Expected To Close In 2027
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 2:23 PM
PHINIA Acquires FMP Group’s Asia-Pacific Brake Parts Business In $160 Million Deal Expected To Close In 2027
PHINIA has agreed to acquire the core operating assets and brand rights of FMP Group’s automotive aftermarket business in Australia, Thailand and Malaysia for approximately $160 million. The deal would expand PHINIA’s brake components portfolio and give it the right to use the Bendix brand in Australia and certain other Asia-Pacific markets.
Brake Components For A Range Of Vehicle Types
FMP designs, manufactures and sells brake components for passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, motorcycles and specialty applications. The acquisition would give PHINIA established relationships with customers in the region and expand its range of products that can be used across different propulsion types.
The assets include in-house product development, testing, manufacturing and distribution capabilities. PHINIA expects the addition of FMP’s engineering team to speed up brake product development, support expansion into related categories and help it sell aftermarket products in more markets. The Bendix rights also give PHINIA an established brand among mechanics and distributors in the markets covered by the agreement.
Expected Financial Contribution And Closing Conditions
PHINIA expects the acquired operations to contribute approximately $120 million in annual revenue and $23 million in annual adjusted EBITDA. It also expects the deal to increase earnings and plans to fund the purchase with available liquidity.
Under the asset purchase agreement, PHINIA will assume specified liabilities associated with the acquired operations. Historical asbestos liabilities and certain other legacy liabilities of the sellers are excluded. The company expects the deal to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, confirmatory insolvency proceedings and other customary closing conditions.
PHINIA is headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan. Its existing businesses include fuel systems, electrical systems, precision-machined components and aftermarket products. The company employs approximately 13,500 people across more than 40 locations in 21 countries.
KEY QUOTE :
“In line with our stated strategy, we continue to be disciplined and focused on acquisitions that strengthen our business at the right price. This transaction meets that standard and is an attractive business acquired at a compelling valuation. This acquisition gives our aftermarket business a strong regional platform, while preserving the financial flexibility to support our other capital allocation priorities. We look forward to welcoming the FMP Group team to PHINIA.”
Brady Ericson, President And Chief Executive Officer Of PHINIA

articles.title: Definity Financial Raises Travelers Synergy Target to $125 Million, Eyes Top-Three Spot
articles.snippet: Definity Financial Raises Travelers Synergy Target to $125 Million, Eyes Top-Three Spot TradingView
articles.text:
News
/ MarketBeat
/ Definity Financial Raises Travelers Synergy Target to $125 Million, Eyes Top-Three Spot
Definity Financial Raises Travelers Synergy Target to $125 Million, Eyes Top-Three Spot
3 min read
Definity Financial (TSE:DFY) is slightly ahead of its long-term growth plan as it integrates its Travelers acquisition and pursues a place among Canada’s top three property and casualty insurers, CEO and President Rowan Saunders said.
Saunders said Definity has reached its initial goal of becoming a top-five insurer and wants to grow organically at roughly twice the industry rate while using acquisitions to expand further. The company has also maintained its core business performance during the integration, he said.
Travelers integration and returns
Saunders described the Travelers acquisition as transformational and said operational progress was slightly ahead of expectations. Definity raised its anticipated synergies from CAD 100 million to CAD 125 million and has already triggered 45% of that amount, he said.
The CEO confirmed that shutting down the remaining Travelers systems is the next major integration milestone. He said Definity expects to complete that work by the end of 2027.
Saunders said the biggest positive surprise was how well Definity’s technology platforms handled the transfer. He said brokers had described it as an unusually smooth acquisition, which helps retain business and realize synergies.
One less favorable development was that the acquired portfolio had contracted from approximately CAD 1.6 billion when discussions began to about CAD 1.5 billion when the deal was completed. Saunders said pricing actions taken before closing should earn through over time, although they came with some revenue cost.
Over the next three to four years, Saunders said he would judge the deal by whether Definity retains and expands its market share and brings the acquired business’s combined ratio, which was roughly 100, down to the low 90s. He said the acquisition is also expected to lift operating return on equity by more than a couple of hundred basis points.
Growth and acquisition priorities
Definity’s long-term ambition is to reach at least 15% market share, up from approximately 5% a couple of years ago. Saunders said Travelers moved the company a couple of percentage points toward that goal.
Canada remains the principal focus for acquisitions, he said, because transactions within the market are easier to integrate. Definity would prioritize commercial and specialty insurance, although it would also consider a large acquisition spanning multiple product lines.
The company is reducing personal auto’s share of its portfolio, from about 55% before its strategic shift to 41% now, with a further decline into the high 30s envisioned. Saunders said the Travelers acquisition advanced Definity’s commercial capabilities by at least five years, but that there is room to grow in areas including specialty financial lines and ocean marine.
After spending CAD 3.3 billion on Travelers, Definity had CAD 1.2 billion of financial capacity, Saunders said. He added that the company continues to make broker-platform acquisitions and evaluate other opportunities.
